title: Quantile Remap Calibration for Precipitation Nowcasting

contributions.purpose: Identify and validate the dominant failure mode behind CSI gaps in deterministic precipitation nowcasting.
contributions.mechanism: Near-miss analysis of false negatives at heavy-rain thresholds, testing whether predictions fall just below the threshold due to intensity underestimation.
contributions.evaluation: 38.6% of false negatives at threshold 219 (heavy rain) are intensity near-misses (predictions in [181, 219)); intensity underestimation accounts for 71.1% of all false negatives.
contributions.source_quote: We identify intensity underestimation as a key failure mode in deterministic nowcasting models and validate this through near-miss analysis showing 38.6% of false negatives are intensity near-misses.

contributions.purpose: Provide a training-free post-hoc method that corrects systematic intensity underestimation.
contributions.mechanism: QRC applies a simple monotone quantile mapping from predicted intensity quantiles to observed quantiles, correcting marginal miscalibration without modifying spatial structure.
contributions.evaluation: On SEVIR, improves CSI-M-POOL16 by 12.6% (0.4660 to 0.5249) and CSI-219-POOL16 by 29.2% (0.2083 to 0.2692).
contributions.source_quote: We propose QRC, a simple monotone quantile mapping that improves CSI-M-POOL16 by 12.6% and CSI-219-POOL16 by 29.2% on the SEVIR benchmark.

contributions.purpose: Show post-hoc calibration can rival expensive generative post-processing without retraining.
contributions.mechanism: Compares uncalibrated EarthFormer + QRC against the CasCast cascaded-diffusion model on CSI-M-POOL16.
contributions.evaluation: QRC closes 104% of the gap between uncalibrated EarthFormer and CasCast on CSI-M-POOL16, using only post-hoc calibration without model retraining.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that QRC closes 104% of the gap between uncalibrated EarthFormer and CasCast on CSI-M-POOL16, using only post-hoc calibration without model retraining.

contributions.purpose: Characterize the tradeoff QRC induces between threshold-based and continuous metrics.
contributions.mechanism: Analyzes CSI (threshold-based) versus CRPS (continuous) and evaluates a blending strategy.
contributions.evaluation: Blending mitigates CRPS degradation while maintaining most CSI gains.
contributions.source_quote: We analyze the trade-off between threshold-based (CSI) and continuous (CRPS) metrics, showing that blending mitigates degradation while maintaining most CSI gains.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work differs by focusing on post-hoc calibration of intensity values rather than probabilities, using quantile mapping to correct systematic marginal miscalibration.
